inputs.userGoal: Migrate the complete hybridcloudworks.com workload from Personal-Site_HCW into this repository using a cost-conscious, five-pillar Azure architecture, Azure Verified Modules, Terraform, and GitHub-first delivery.
subGoals: Cost-conscious production foundation with a USD 150 monthly budget ceiling and one production workload state.
Security-first admin plane using Microsoft Entra ID, managed identities, least privilege, and no static Azure credentials.
Static-first public delivery with measurable reliability and a staged Firebase-to-Azure rollback boundary.

reasoning.whyChosen: Creates one production workload, cost, policy, and access boundary.
reasoning.tradeoffs: A single workload group is simpler and cheaper to operate, but service-level lifecycle separation is handled through Terraform modules and identities instead of resource groups.

resources.name: stapp-hcw-prod

properties.adminShell: Publicly downloadable SPA with all data and mutations protected by the API

reasoning.whyChosen: Preserves the static-first public site, global delivery, preview capability, managed TLS, and predictable low baseline cost.
alternativesConsidered: Azure Front Door plus Blob Storage
reasoning.tradeoffs: Static Web Apps remains publicly reachable. Cloudflare provides the initial edge control, while origin-bypass risk is mitigated through API authentication and documented for later hardening.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Hosted in the workload resource group and deployed from the protected GitHub production workflow.

properties.connectivity: VNet integration for Flex Consumption outbound; PaaS services protected by service firewalls scoped to Functions outbound IPs
properties.networkingDecision: ADR-001 (2026-07-30): Private Endpoints deferred indefinitely. Service firewalls + managed identity is the accepted security model. Threat of network-adjacent attackers inside a corporate estate does not apply to a single-operator content site.

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides a durable outbound network boundary for serverless compute. PaaS service firewalls restrict inbound to Functions VNet integration IPs at no additional cost.
alternativesConsidered: Private endpoints for every PaaS service
reasoning.tradeoffs: Service firewalls are less isolated than Private Link at the network layer but the threat model does not require Private Link isolation. Managed identity remains the primary auth control regardless of network path.

reasoning.whyChosen: Flex Consumption requires a subnet delegated to Microsoft.App/environments with at least a /27; /24 leaves capacity for all three apps.
reasoning.tradeoffs: The shared subnet is cheaper and large enough, but the apps share the platform networking gateway pool.

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides pay-per-use scaling, VNet integration, and zone support for public and admin HTTP APIs.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Flex has no deployment slots; releases require artifact promotion, health validation, and an explicit rollback package.

resources.name: func-hcw-api-prod-9x7k

properties.authentication: Entra validation for admin routes; anonymous public routes explicitly allowlisted and rate-limited
properties.credentials: Managed identity only for Azure data plane

reasoning.whyChosen: Separates request-response APIs from privileged background integrations and preserves independent scaling and blast radius.
reasoning.tradeoffs: A separate app adds deployment and monitoring objects but prevents background secrets and broad permissions from being exposed to the public API process.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Requires a Flex plan, isolated host storage, telemetry, data access, and narrowly scoped secret access.

reasoning.whyChosen: Isolates timers, queues, change feed processing, AI calls, and third-party integrations from internet-facing APIs.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Additional application lifecycle, but no fixed always-ready charge and materially smaller credential blast radius.

properties.deliverySemantics: At-least-once with idempotency keys, bounded retries, and poison queues

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides a retry-safe execution boundary for publishing, ingestion, AI, media, Publer, Plaud, Telegram, Klaviyo, Linkie, GitHub, and other integrations.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Storage Queues are cheaper than Service Bus but require application-owned idempotency and do not provide rich broker features.

reasoning.whyChosen: Creates a separate trust and scaling boundary for untrusted lab job submission and Hostinger agent coordination.
alternativesConsidered: Run labs in the main API
reasoning.tradeoffs: Hostinger remains an external reliability dependency; Azure only brokers jobs and never opens inbound access to the VPS.

reasoning.whyChosen: Prevents anonymous or semi-trusted lab traffic from sharing permissions with the editorial and publishing system.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Public lab access requires stronger application-layer abuse controls because API Management is deferred.

properties.publicNetworkAccess: Enabled; restricted to Functions VNet integration subnet outbound IPs via service firewall
properties.networkControl: Service firewall — allow snet-functions-integration CIDR; deny all other public access
diagnostics: Query and partition metrics without document bodies
properties.containerDesignGate: Partition keys and containers require query-contract inventory; do not copy existing Terraform one-for-one

reasoning.whyChosen: Matches the low, spiky document workload while supporting managed identity, change feed processing, and pay-per-request billing.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Serverless is single-region and cannot add regions. A future multiregion requirement needs a controlled migration to provisioned or autoscale throughput.

resources.name: sthcwcontentprod9x7k
resources.subtype: Content, media, queue, and migration storage

properties.publicNetworkAccess: Enabled; restricted to Functions VNet integration subnet outbound IPs via storage firewall
properties.networkControl: Storage firewall — allow snet-functions-integration CIDR for Blob and Queue; deny all other public access

reasoning.whyChosen: ZRS provides inexpensive zone durability for media and durable asynchronous work while managed identity eliminates storage keys.
reasoning.tradeoffs: ZRS costs more than LRS but avoids a zone-level storage dependency; regional recovery still depends on backup/export procedures.

reasoning.whyChosen: Isolates API host state and supports zone-aware Functions.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Adds one low-volume account but prevents host-state and permission coupling.

reasoning.whyChosen: Isolates worker host state and supports zone-aware Functions.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Adds one low-volume account but prevents host-state and permission coupling.

reasoning.whyChosen: Isolates labs host state and supports zone-aware Functions.

properties.publicNetworkAccess: Enabled; restricted to Functions VNet integration subnet outbound IPs via Key Vault firewall
properties.networkControl: Key Vault firewall — allow snet-functions-integration CIDR; trusted-services bypass enabled for Azure Monitor

reasoning.whyChosen: Centralizes third-party secrets with recovery protection, managed-identity access, and auditable least privilege.
reasoning.tradeoffs: One vault is operationally simple; per-app RBAC and secret naming boundaries limit blast radius until multiple vaults are justified.

properties.provisioning: Feature-gated until model capacity, content filter, and budget allocation are approved
properties.modelDeployments: Pinned model names and versions supplied as approved variables

reasoning.whyChosen: Replaces Vertex AI as the Azure-native default while preserving the source system's provider-adapter contract and cost controls.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Model capacity and version availability are regional and time-sensitive; AI is not a hard dependency for public rendering.

properties.tablePlans: Analytics for security and application failures; Basic or Auxiliary only after query requirements are verified

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides centralized, queryable telemetry with explicit ingestion and retention cost controls.
reasoning.tradeoffs: A daily cap can delay telemetry during an incident; cap alerts and sampling must fire before the limit is reached.

reasoning.whyChosen: Separates API health and deployment signals while consolidating storage in one workspace.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Adds configuration but materially improves component ownership and rollback evidence.

reasoning.whyChosen: Separates worker and integration health from request-response API telemetry.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Adds configuration but makes background failures and retry behavior directly observable.

reasoning.whyChosen: Keeps semi-trusted lab and agent health separate from editorial operations.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Adds configuration but improves abuse and sandbox operational visibility.

properties.federation: GitHub pull-request or protected workflow subject
properties.roleBoundary: Reader plus narrowly scoped state read access

reasoning.whyChosen: Removes long-lived Azure credentials and keeps pull-request planning read-only.
reasoning.tradeoffs: OIDC trust and bootstrap RBAC remain a separately approved administrative step.

properties.roleBoundary: Workload deployment permissions; cannot change bootstrap trust or grant itself RBAC

reasoning.whyChosen: Separates mutation authority from planning and binds it to the protected production environment.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Bootstrap must grant exact resource deployment roles before routine delivery can operate.

properties.receivers: Parameterized owner email and optional webhook

reasoning.whyChosen: Gives reliability, security, and budget signals an explicit owner and delivery route.
reasoning.tradeoffs: One group is simple; notification fan-out can be split if ownership grows.

reasoning.whyChosen: Turns the approved ceiling into an operating control and makes cost ownership queryable from first deployment.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Budgets alert but do not stop spend; AI quotas, telemetry caps, lifecycle policies, and operator response remain required.

resources.name: cloudflare-hcw-prod
resources.subtype: Authoritative DNS, CDN, TLS, and edge controls

controls: WAF managed rules where plan permits

reasoning.whyChosen: Preserves the current edge with materially lower fixed cost than Azure Front Door Standard or Premium.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Cloudflare cannot provide Azure Private Link origin isolation; public origin hardening and API authentication remain essential.

overallReasoning.summary: The target is a static-first Azure workload with an anonymous public plane, Entra-protected admin plane, isolated serverless execution boundaries, identity-based data access, durable asynchronous workflows, centralized observability, and GitHub-governed delivery. The design preserves the complete source workload through migration domains rather than treating the incomplete existing Azure attempt as authoritative.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: The USD 150 ceiling intentionally defers Azure Front Door, Azure Firewall, NAT Gateway, API Management, multiregion data, always-ready compute, and Private Link (ADR-001, 2026-07-30: service firewalls are the accepted network control for a single-operator content site — no corporate estate, no network-adjacent threat model). Cloudflare remains the edge. Cosmos DB Serverless accepts a regional-outage limitation and does not support availability zones — AZ redundancy is removed. PaaS services are protected by service firewalls scoped to the Functions VNet integration subnet; managed identity is the primary auth boundary. Isolated Function host storage remains public at the platform level and contains only host and deployment state. Azure OpenAI is feature-gated until capacity and budget are confirmed. Only one production workload state is planned; bootstrap identity and state trust remain a separate administrative lifecycle boundary.

plan.validation: The draft topology has coherent compute, storage, identity, networking, observability, and delivery dependencies. Region-specific SKU availability, Azure OpenAI capacity, Cosmos partition keys, exact AVM module versions, and monthly list-price calculations must be verified before IaC generation.
architecturePrinciples: Static first: public browsing does not depend on live database reads or AI availability.
Identity first: managed identity and Entra RBAC replace service keys wherever supported.
Least privilege by execution boundary: API, background work, and labs do not share broad identities.
Async side effects: external publishing and notifications are retry-safe, idempotent, observable, and poison-queue protected.
Cost is a design constraint: serverless capacity, bounded telemetry, lifecycle policies, quotas, tags, and budgets are code.
One reviewed artifact moves forward: GitHub plan, approval, apply, deployment, and rollback evidence remain connected.
Migration is reversible until acceptance gates pass; Firebase decommissioning is a separate approval.
